content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge relies on Matthew 1:16's withheld active begetting verb, i.e. a single verse's non-statement, as support for holding the defense's chain.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"The text states that before Mary and Joseph came together she was found with child of the Holy Ghost ([L1] Matthew 1:18, 20), with the active begetting verb withheld from Joseph in the record of the generations ([L2] egennēthē in Matthew 1:16).","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.","room":"a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS — read to forbid using Matthew 1:16's withheld begat verb as support for the defense's holding, versus read to forbid only a holding that expressly rests on one verse's silence alone.","why":"The judge treats the absence of an active begetting verb from Matthew 1:16 as a reason supporting the defense, which is a single verse's non-statement grounding STANDS."}
